metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.7) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly above recent highs.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct — reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (e.g., < -0.5) and price is trending up, model often overcorrects — cap forecast at recent peak or adjust downward 3–5%.
- Model consistently underestimates true price peaks in 30-day horizon — add 2–5% buffer to forecast if recent 7-day average is rising.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings (e.g., +0.7, -0.7, +0.7), model tends to lag — forecast 1–2 days ahead of actual turning point.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed, model often fails to capture mean reversion — if price is above 30-day moving average, reduce forecast by 1–3% per day until reversion.
- If true outcome shows sudden drop after spike, model often fails to anticipate — add 1–3% downward adjustment in next 3–5 days if sentiment turns negative.
- Model underestimates volatility in sentiment-driven markets — if sentiment swings >0.5 in 3 consecutive days, increase forecast variance by 1–2% for next 5 days.
